title: DataRace ending crowns the sticky order's leader, not the largest final value
body:
## Summary
computeTimingPlan applied the moving average + 6 % hysteresis to the last period too, so the ending crowned an entity whose final value was not the largest.

## Description
The plan's order is calmed for the viewer (timing-plan-first step 4: order by a moving average + hysteresis, keep bar values raw). The ending reads that order as the result: WinnerSpotlight renders "NO. 1 AT THE END" for `winnerId = plan.orders[last][0]` (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:280, packages/compositions/src/DataRace/ending.tsx:56), generation rule 4's winnerOf uses the same index (packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:216) and the MCP tool returns it as final_order (apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts:111). A title decided in the final period by less than the margin therefore crowned the runner-up while the bars showed the winner's larger raw value - an output that outruns its evidence. Fixed: the last period's #1 is the largest raw final value (ties keep the viewer's order; the rest of the order is untouched) at packages/compositions/src/timing/plan.ts:195.

## Flow
- compute_timing_plan over a season whose leader changes in the last round by < 6 % (F1 2010: Alonso led before the final, Vettel won 256 to 252)
- stickyOrders keeps the earlier leader on top for the last period
- the spotlight crowns that entity 'NO. 1 AT THE END' with a smaller value than a dimmed bar above it

## Expected impact
Every viewer of a close-finish race video; a wrong champion on a published video is the most damaging error the format can make. Could break: nothing for plans whose final leader already matches - both committed fixtures are byte-identical.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the crowned #1 is the entity with the largest final value
Before: F1 2010 walked through the plan (default opts and rankSmooth 1) crowned Webber 242 while Vettel had 256; 2007 crowned Hamilton 109 over Raikkonen 110; new test red
After: 2010 crowns Vettel 256, 2007 Raikkonen 110 under both opts; the test is green for {}, rankSmooth 1, a 20 % hysteresis and no hysteresis
Method: gate - red-then-green unit test plus a probe over two real season finals
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/compositions/src/timing/plan.ts:190 (before) orders[P-1] from stickyOrders
packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:280 winnerId: plan.orders[last]?.[0]
packages/schemas/src/generation-rules.ts:216 const id = last?.[0];
probe before: {} plan final order: webber,alonso,vettel,hamilton | raw final order: vettel,alonso,webber,hamilton
probe after:  {} plan final order: vettel,webber,alonso,hamilton
instrument: timing.test.ts 'the race ends on the truth' (seeded red before the fix)

title: DataRace hook under 36 frames never shows its question
body:
## Summary
dataRaceState hard-coded a 60-frame hook, so hooks of 1-35 frames rendered a blank first frame and hook 36 popped off in one frame.

## Description
compute_timing_plan accepts opts.hookFrames 0-300 (apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts:37). The hook opacity was `1 - clamp01((frame - 36) / (hook_end - 36))` and the chart `clamp01((frame - 24) / 36)` (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:252-256 before): for hook_end < 36 the divisor is negative and the hook is 0 from frame 0, so the first frame is a bare sheet with a title (the golden path: the video is judged in the first frame); hook_end = 36 divides by zero; hookFrames 0 hides the first 24 frames of data time. Fixed: both windows scale into hook_end below the 60-frame default, unchanged at 60+ (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:256-264).

## Flow
- the co-pilot calls compute_timing_plan with opts.hookFrames 30 to shorten a video into the 30-90 s band
- dataRaceState(frame 0) -> hookOpacity 0, chartOpacity 0
- the video opens on an empty sheet; the question hook is never seen

## Expected impact
Viewers of any short-hook video lose the hook entirely; the first frame (thumbnail-adjacent) is empty. Could break: nothing at hook >= 60 (curves pinned, golden hashes unchanged).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the hook question is on screen at frame 0 for every allowed hook length
Before: hookFrames 20/30 -> frame 0 hook 0.00 chart 0.00; hookFrames 0 -> chart 0.00 at frame 0; test red
After: hookFrames 20/30/36/40/60/300 -> hook 1 at frame 0, 0 at hook_end, chart 1 at hook_end, no step > 0.2; hookFrames 0 -> chart 1 at frame 0
Method: gate - red-then-green test over six hook lengths plus a probe
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
before: packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:256 const hookOpacity = frame < s.hook_end ? 1 - clamp01((frame - 36) / (s.hook_end - 36)) : 0;
apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts:37 hookFrames: z.number().int().min(0).max(300)
probe before: hookFrames=30 f0: hook=0.00 chart=0.00
probe after:  hookFrames=30 f0: hook=1.00 chart=0.00 | f29: hook=0.08 chart=0.94
instrument: DataRace.test.tsx 'a hook of any allowed length' (seeded red)

title: A DataRace card pushed past depth 3 vanishes in one frame
body:
## Summary
When a fourth event card overlapped, the oldest card was dropped at full opacity the frame its depth reached 3.

## Description
dataRaceState skipped any card with `depth >= CARD.maxDepth` (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:232) while its opacity was still 1, so the buried card blinked out mid-entrance of the newcomer. event-card-stack: 'each card exits on its own clock, even from under the pile; cap the visible depth at 3'. Fixed: opacity also scales by clamp01(maxDepth - depth) (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:248), so it fades over the newcomer's 6-frame ramp.

## Flow
- four events whose 120-frame lives overlap (12 events allowed)
- the fourth card's vis ramps 0 -> 1 over 6 frames; the oldest card's depth reaches 3
- the oldest card disappears from 1.00 to 0.00 in one frame

## Expected impact
Viewers see a pop in the busiest beat of the video. Could break: nothing - the sample never stacks four cards; golden hashes unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no card leaves the stack by a one-frame jump
Before: 4 cards 20 f apart -> 'free-tier at 366: 1.00 -> 0.00'; sample + a 4th card -> 'outage at 641: 1.00 -> 0.00'
After: both probes: no per-frame opacity drop > 0.3; the 3-deep depth test still holds
Method: gate - red-then-green test plus probe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: DataRace.test.tsx 'a card pushed past the depth cap fades out' (seeded red)

title: DataRace safe-box test asserted a constant instead of the frame
body:
## Summary
'keeps text inside the safe box' measured only the smallest top over 100 px on one frame and then asserted `1544 + 34 <= 1580`.

## Description
packages/compositions/src/DataRace/DataRace.test.tsx:436-437 (before) never measured a bottom edge: any box above y 100 was filtered out and the bottom check was arithmetic on literals - green since written (test-harness / negative-control-tests). legibility-floor requires content inside the safe box. The test now walks the markup of the hook, mid-race, every card frame, the last timeline frame and the spotlight, checks every box positioned against the frame (top and bottom), the transformed card stack and the sample badge, and asserts it reached > 10 boxes per frame (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/DataRace.test.tsx:482-522).

## Flow
- seed footerBottom 1600 or cardTop 1450 in layout.ts
- old test: green; new test: red naming the box and frame
- seeds reverted; the real frame passes

## Expected impact
Future layout changes that push text into the platform UI band are caught by the suite instead of on a phone. Could break: nothing (test only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the safe-box test catches a box outside y 150-1580
Before: 0 of 2 seeded violations caught
After: 2 of 2 caught ('frame 0: box 1568-1600 ...', 'frame 554: card outage 1450-1628')
Method: gate - seeded violations on both sides
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A font that fails to load cancels the render without naming itself
body:
## Summary
loadFonts rethrew the browser's FontFace rejection under Promise.all, so the render died with 'A network error occurred.' and no [statreel-fonts] report line.

## Description
packages/compositions/src/fonts.ts:79-110 (before): the first failing face rejected Promise.all, cancelRender received the raw DOMException (no family, weight or file) and the report line - the only machine record of which faces loaded - was never printed. seek-stable-composition-authoring: refuse where it is configured 'with an error that names it'. Fixed: loads settle together, each failure is rethrown naming family, weight and file, the report is logged with every failed face, then the render is cancelled (packages/compositions/src/fonts.ts:80-115).

## Flow
- a woff2 asset is missing from the bundle or blocked
- FontFace.load rejects with Chrome's generic NetworkError
- the operator sees 'A network error occurred.' in the failed render with nothing to act on

## Expected impact
Operator diagnosing a failed render gets the face and file at once. Could break: nothing on the success path (report, then continueRender).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a font failure leaves a named error and a report
Before: cancelRender got 'A network error occurred.'; no report line
After: cancelRender gets 'OFL font Inter 100 900 (fonts/inter/Inter-Variable.woff2) failed to load: A network error occurred.'; report failed ['Inter 100 900'], check.Inter false
Method: gate - red-then-green test with stubbed FontFace/document/remotion
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
before packages/compositions/src/fonts.ts:92 throw err;
before packages/compositions/src/fonts.ts:110 .catch((err: unknown) => cancelRender(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err))));

title: A narrow event dwell on period 0 turns the timing plan into NaN
body:
## Summary
An event on the first period with a small spread underflowed its Gaussian dwell weights to zero; 0 / 0 made every knot NaN.

## Description
packages/compositions/src/timing/plan.ts:247 (before) normalised the dwell bump by its sum; period 0 is forced to weight 0, so an event there with spread < ~0.026 (compute_timing_plan allows any positive spread, apps/server/src/generation/mcp-tools.ts:31) gave bs = 0. The plan was written with null knots, the tool returned ok: true with its sha, and the failure surfaced later as 'knots must increase'. Fixed: when the bump underflows, the dwell lands on the first period with frames (packages/compositions/src/timing/plan.ts:256).

## Flow
- compute_timing_plan with events [{ period: 0, spread: 0.02 }]
- bump sum 0 -> frames NaN -> knots NaN -> JSON null
- validate_generation_output reports an unrelated knots rule

## Expected impact
The co-pilot gets a usable plan instead of a silently broken one. Could break: nothing - other spreads and periods give identical plans.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every accepted input yields a finite, schema-valid plan
Before: last knot NaN, event frame NaN, TimingPlanSchema false
After: last knot 720 = timeline_end, event frame 60, schema true
Method: gate - red-then-green test over 3 periods x 3 spreads
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
before packages/compositions/src/timing/plan.ts:246-247 bump = ... (i === 0 ? 0 : exp(...)); const bs = bump.reduce(...)
probe before: spread 0.02 period 0: last knot NaN ... schema false
instrument: timing.test.ts 'an event's dwell always lands' (seeded red)

title: Settle the whole final DataRace order to raw values (rows below the crown)
body:
## Summary
After 0eb3254 only the crown is guaranteed; the rest of the final order can still show a row above a larger value in the spotlight frame.

## Description
plan.orders[last] below #1 still comes from the moving average + hysteresis (packages/compositions/src/timing/plan.ts:190-196). The spotlight keeps every row on screen dimmed to 20 % with its raw value label (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/DataRaceFrame.tsx spotlight branch), so a #2 shown below a smaller #3 is a visible contradiction in the final frame. Releasing the smoothing for the whole last period (raw sort, ties by the viewer's order) changes the sample plan (its final order differs from raw below #4), so the committed fixtures and golden hashes must be regenerated - director-owned, hence Lane B.

## Flow
- fix: orders[P-1] = stable raw sort of orders[P-1]
- regenerate fixtures (WRITE_FIXTURES=1 ...write-fixtures.test.ts) and the inline golden hashes
- measure: rows above a larger raw value in the final period, before vs after, on the sample and the real-F1 fixture

## Expected impact
Viewers of the ending see a final table consistent with its numbers. Could break: golden hashes and the sample plan sha (expected, regen).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the final frame's order agrees with its values
Before: sample: final order != raw order (top 4 equal, lower rows differ); 2010 walk after 0eb3254: Webber 242 above Alonso 246
After: predicted 0 rows above a larger value in the final period; not built this round (fixture regen is director-owned)
Method: probe - plan final order vs raw sort on the sample and the F1 2010 walk
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe: sample final==raw: false prism,zephyr,lumen,pixelo | prism,zephyr,lumen,pixelo
probe 2010 after 0eb3254: plan final order vettel,webber,alonso,hamilton | raw vettel,alonso,webber,hamilton
instrument: count of final-period rows sitting above a larger raw value (sample: final order != raw order below #4); needs the director-owned fixture regen: WRITE_FIXTURES=1 npx vitest run packages/compositions/src/DataRace/write-fixtures.test.ts, then update the DataRace golden hashes

title: TIMING.md says every card lives 120 frames; props allow 105-135
body:

## Description

## Flow
- an event sets life_frames 105
- TIMING.md still says 120
- a reviewer checks the wrong exit frame

## Expected impact
Reviewers of timing notes. Could break: the TIMING.md fixture (regen).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the timing note states the card-life rule the composition applies
Before: 1 sentence asserting a fixed 120-frame life
After: 0 (predicted; not built - regen is director-owned)
Method: probe - the sentence read against the schema limits and state.ts
Result: better
Gate: none

title: axis_max below the data maximum clips DataRace bars to equal full length
body:
## Summary
A fixed axis_max lower than the largest value makes every bar above it full width while their labels show different numbers.

## Description
axisMaxAt returns props.axis_max unchanged (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:138) and BarRow clamps `Math.min(1, row.value / axisMax)` (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/parts.tsx:157). The schema accepts any positive axis_max (packages/schemas/src/data-race.ts:189) and no cross-field rule compares it with the values - the golden path's 'trick axis' anti-pattern. The check belongs in the schema's superRefine (or generation rules), which this context does not own.

## Flow
- the co-pilot sets axis_max: 100 for a share series that peaks at 104
- every bar over 100 renders at full width
- two leaders look tied while their labels differ

## Expected impact
Viewers misread the race; a reviewer sees nothing wrong in the props. Could break: props that set a cap below their data (rejected with a clear message).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no bar is clipped by the axis
Before: simulation: 3 walked cases (share 104 % vs cap 100; cumulative points past a hand cap; a cap copied from an earlier season)
After: predicted: all three rejected at validation
Method: simulation - the seam is in packages/schemas (another context)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/compositions/src/DataRace/state.ts:138 if (props.axis_max !== undefined) return Math.max(props.axis_max, 1e-9);
packages/compositions/src/DataRace/parts.tsx:157 const w = Math.max(6, Math.min(1, row.value / axisMax) * L.barMaxW);
instrument: schema/generation-rules test: props with axis_max < max(values) rejected (red before), owned by Schemas & Contracts (superRefine) - out-of-scope seam

title: axis_max schema description still says the axis follows the current leader
body:

A model reading the stale sentence may set axis_max to avoid a rescaling that no longer happens.

## Evaluation

title: Memoize DataRace text layouts per frame
body:
## Summary
Every frame re-measures the title, hook, names, clock and footer; caching them looked like a render saving.

## Description
DataRaceFrame calls clockLayout, titleLayout (twice), hookLayout, footerLayout, unitLayout and nameLayout/hookTileNameLayout per entity on every frame (packages/compositions/src/DataRace/DataRaceFrame.tsx, packages/compositions/src/DataRace/layout.ts). Measured, they cost 0.20 ms of a 1.08 ms server-side render per frame; a browser frame capture costs tens of milliseconds, so the saving does not reach the render time.

## Flow
- time renderToStaticMarkup over every sample frame
- time the layout calls alone
- compare with the render's per-frame capture cost

## Expected impact
None measurable. Could break: a cache keyed wrongly would break seek stability.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - render time per frame
Before: 1.08 ms/frame SSR, of which layouts 0.20 ms (clockLayout 0.11)
After: at best 0.88 ms/frame SSR against a >= 30 ms browser capture per frame
Method: probe - timed path over 1230 frames
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: frames 1230: markup 1.079 ms/frame, state 0.017, layouts 0.202 (clockLayout 0.106)
instrument: per-frame SSR timing over all 1230 sample frames
